answer: Why do clone farms stay cheap? Because identity is free to mint. Globe maker inked survey record filed with the chart house changes that arithmetic: each inked survey is a coastal chart countersigned by the warden, so a farm must assemble a hundred real globes by hand, so the kernel for each fake is paid in the real world. A single honest agent crosses this gate in seconds; a farm crosses it a hundred times, and the summit of those crossings is a bill no payout covers. The quartz is that the same proof cannot serve two names.
